content: Adalimumab is a medication that can increase your susceptibility to infections or worsen existing infections. Avoid close contact with individuals who have contagious illnesses such as chickenpox, COVID-19, measles, or the flu. Inform your healthcare provider that you are using adalimumab before receiving any vaccinations or immunizations. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used if absolutely necessary, as it may pose risks to an unborn baby. Discuss the potential risks and benefits with your doctor. Adalimumab can also pass into breast milk, so consult your healthcare provider if you are breastfeeding. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a detailed list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs, as well as herbal supplements, and share this information with your doctor and pharmacist. If someone overdoses on this medication and experiences severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. In the U.S., you can call 1-800-222-1222. While using adalimumab, regular laboratory and medical tests, such as complete blood counts and liver function tests, are necessary to monitor your condition and detect any potential side effects. If you miss a dose, consult your doctor or pharmacist promptly to establish a new dosing schedule. Store this medication in the refrigerator and do not freeze it. Keep it in its original container to protect it from light. Some brands may also be stored at room temperature for a limited time—check with your pharmacist or the product packaging for specific instructions. Discard any unused portion of the medication properly. Do not flush it down the toilet or pour it into a drain unless instructed to do so. Adalimumab may rarely cause serious, potentially fatal liver disease in individuals exposed to the hepatitis B virus. Your doctor may order blood tests and monitor for symptoms during treatment and for several months after your last dose. Serious allergic reactions to this medication are rare but possible. If you experience any unusual symptoms, contact your healthcare provider immediately. This medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Common side effects may include redness, itching, pain, or swelling at the injection site. To minimize these effects, rotate injection sites and avoid injecting into areas of sore, bruised, red, or hardened skin. Do not rub the injection site after administering the medication to reduce the risk of bruising. Before using adalimumab, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, any of its components, or other adalimumab products. This medication may contain inactive ingredients, such as natural rubber or latex, which can cause allergic reactions or other issues. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete information about this medication and your specific health needs. This document is a summary and does not include all possible information about adalimumab. It is not a substitute for professional medical advice. For any concerns or questions, contact your healthcare provider.
